title: Repeated client certificate verification allows excessive CPU consumption during DTLS handshakes
summary: While waiting for Finished, additional handshake traffic could make the server revisit cached Certificate, ClientKeyExchange, and CertificateVerify messages. This repeats parsing and cryptographic/certificate-chain verification depending on policy; a malicious client can withhold Finished and send more traffic to consume CPU. Pion WebRTC is affected when operating as DTLS server.
ai_role: The Pion maintainer's case-specific advisory credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier E9EALMAT). It does not identify model versions or internal discovery dates.
classification_note: The cited advisory documents public disclosure; it does not establish whether defenders knew of the issue or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: The advisory identifies fix commit 979ad79d and the following package-version scope: v1 1.2.2–1.5.4 and v2 2.0.0–2.2.12 (no patched versions listed); v3 before 3.1.13, fixed 3.1.13. This source does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: repeated or concurrent handshakes can consume CPU and delay legitimate connections under the stated server role.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible attack path but does not report observed exploitation.
